sourceTitle: City of Vancouver Visual Standards Guide, updated February 2018
regionUnits: PDF points from the page's top-left, as MuPDF's SVG output places them

extractions.where: the colour emblem

adoption.label: 18 July 2006
adoption.note: The guide records that the emblem was designed by the City’s in-house graphic designer, Elaine Ayres, and adopted unanimously by Council on 18 July 2006.

source.title: City of Vancouver Visual Standards Guide, February 2018, PDF page 4

extractions.notes: The City emblem in colour, for white or very light grounds: two overlapping blue and green forms over “CITY OF VANCOUVER”. The guide reads them as budding blossoms, ocean waves, mountain peaks, birds, the sails of Canada Place and a V for Vancouver.

extractions.where: the solid black emblem

adoption.label: 18 July 2006
adoption.note: The guide records that the emblem was designed by the City’s in-house graphic designer, Elaine Ayres, and adopted unanimously by Council on 18 July 2006.

source.title: City of Vancouver Visual Standards Guide, February 2018, PDF page 4

extractions.notes: The solid black emblem, for light grounds where the colour version cannot be used. Its forms have gaps where the colour emblem’s overlap, and the guide forbids making it by recolouring the colour artwork.

extractions.where: the reversed (white) emblem

adoption.label: 18 July 2006
adoption.note: The guide records that the emblem was designed by the City’s in-house graphic designer, Elaine Ayres, and adopted unanimously by Council on 18 July 2006.

source.title: City of Vancouver Visual Standards Guide, February 2018, PDF page 4

extractions.notes: The reversed emblem in white, for medium to dark grounds, with the same gaps as the black version. The guide’s black backing panel is not part of the artwork.

extractions.where: the colour Engineering Services lockup
extractions.notes: The emblem set with a department name, the only way the guide allows the two to be combined: a thin rule, then “Engineering Services” in blue. Corporate Communications supplies the files on request.

extractions.where: the black Engineering Services lockup
extractions.notes: The same lockup in solid black.

extractions.where: the reversed Engineering Services lockup
extractions.notes: The same lockup reversed in white; the guide’s black panel is not part of the artwork.

extractions.where: the former Engineering Services lockup, inside the “Incorrect usage” box; the guide’s red cross over it is left out
extractions.notes: The earlier department lockup: “Engineering Services” centred under the emblem, beneath a rule. The guide shows it as the former version, replaced when the emblem and department name were updated.

extractions.where: the colour Public Art Program lockup
extractions.notes: The emblem set with a program name: a thin rule, then “Public Art Program” in blue, the guide’s second example of the department lockup.

extractions.where: the black Public Art Program lockup
extractions.notes: The same lockup in solid black.

extractions.where: the reversed Public Art Program lockup
extractions.notes: The same lockup reversed in white; the guide’s black panel is not part of the artwork.

extractions.where: the colour Greenest City lockup
extractions.notes: The Greenest City logo beside the City emblem, the pair the guide supplies as one file: two speech bubbles turned upside down on a base to read as trees, with “GREENEST CITY”. The guide says the logo never appears without the emblem to its left.
extractions.dateNote: Council approved the Greenest City Action Plan in July 2011, as the guide records; the guide does not date the logo. February 2018 is the guide’s date.

extractions.where: the black Greenest City lockup
extractions.notes: The same pair in solid black.

extractions.where: the reversed Greenest City lockup
extractions.notes: The same pair reversed in white; the guide’s black panel is not part of the artwork.

extractions.where: the retired Talk Green to Us bubble, inside the “Incorrect version” box; the guide’s red cross is left out, and so is the lettering of an emblem the page clips away behind it
extractions.notes: A green speech bubble with “TALK GREEN TO US”: the branding of the public engagement that shaped the Greenest City Action Plan. The Greenest City logo kept its bubble.
extractions.dateNote: Talk Green to Us was the engagement that developed the Greenest City Action Plan, which Council approved in July 2011. The guide marks it as no longer in use; it gives no dates for the mark itself.

extractions.where: the retired Greenest City 2020 logo; the guide’s red cross is left out
extractions.notes: The two bubble-trees with “GREENEST CITY 2020”: the plan’s earlier name, with its 2020 target year.

extractions.where: the retired Greenest City 2020 Access to Nature logo; the guide’s red cross is left out
extractions.notes: Greenest City 2020 set in one line with “Access to Nature”, one of the plan’s goal areas, below in blue.

extractions.where: the small rendering of the coat of arms, with “CITY OF VANCOUVER” beneath it, beside the arms text
extractions.notes: The City’s coat of arms as the guide prints it: the shield with ship’s sail and crown, the logger and fisherman supporters, the Kwakwaka’wakw pole and dogwood, and the motto, over “CITY OF VANCOUVER”. The guide reserves the arms for Mayor and Council and formal, ceremonial use.
extractions.dateNote: The guide records that the arms were granted by the College of Arms in London on 31 March 1969. February 2018 is the guide’s date.

extractions.where: the Vancouver Public Library logo in the alignment examples
extractions.notes: V, P and L on tilted blue, red and yellow squares over “Vancouver Public Library” in serif.

extractions.where: the Vancouver Police Department logo in the alignment examples
extractions.notes: The Vancouver Police Department badge over the department’s name and the motto “Beyond the Call”.

extractions.where: the Vancouver Economic Commission logo in the alignment examples
extractions.notes: A V of blue and green stripes over “VANCOUVER” and “ECONOMIC COMMISSION”.

extractions.designLabel: Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation
extractions.where: the Park Board logo in the alignment examples
extractions.notes: “VANCOUVER” over mountains, trees and water, with “BOARD OF PARKS AND RECREATION” on green.

extractions.where: the Fire Rescue Services badge in the alignment examples
extractions.notes: A red cross badge ringed with “VANCOUVER FIRE” and “RESCUE SERVICES”, with firefighting emblems at its centre.

body.notes: The City of Vancouver’s emblem of 2006, from the City’s February 2018 Visual Standards Guide, with the department lockups, the Greenest City logo and the retired marks the guide shows, and the logos of the City’s agencies and boards as the guide pairs them with the emblem. The coat of arms, granted in 1969, is reserved for Mayor and Council and formal occasions; it is in Coats of Arms.
